notes: Identity independently verified from cached article header: title After a pair of self-control-intensive tasks, sucrose swishing improves subsequent working memory performance; Evan C Carter and Michael E McCullough; BMC Psychol, 2013 Oct 30;1(1):22; DOI 10.1186/2050-7283-1-22; PMCID PMC4269986. Supplied text is a primary full-article PMC parse containing Methods, Results, tables, Discussion and references, not an abstract-only excerpt. No PDF supplied. Only unfinished pval_value_r examined; other core fields are unassigned placeholders. The neutral description and p. 4–5 locator do not select among the overall effort main effect, effort-by-rinse interaction, and high-versus-low-effort comparisons within three rinse groups. No rinse group or exact replication test is specified. The article uses a principal-component OSPAN score; it does not report reverse-digit-span or response-inhibition outcome tests. Multiple printed candidate p values cannot be assigned uniquely to this row. Printed candidates (not selected): overall effort F(1,229)=5.86, p<.05 with narrative d=-0.30; effort-by-rinse F(2,229)=3.54, p<.05; unsweetened high-versus-low effort t(48)=-1.76, p=.09, d=.50; sucralose t(90)=-.59, p=.56, d=-.12; sucrose t(91)=-3.05, p=.003, d=.63. These retain the table’s printed signs and precision. No p computed or inferred for the nonsignificant rinse main effect F(2,229)=0.08. No sample-size derivation performed.
